title: Effectiveness and tolerance of antiresorptive drugs in patients with systemic sclerosis and osteoporosis - a prospective multicentre study
summary:
Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune disease that is often accompanied by osteoporosis. Many patients develop reduced bone mineral density at an early stage, which significantly increases the risk of bone fractures. At the same time, many of those affected suffer from gastrointestinal complaints and swallowing disorders, which makes it difficult to take oral osteoporosis medication.
The aim of the study is to investigate the efficacy and tolerability of various osteoporosis-specific therapies in patients with SSc. Particular attention is paid to the comparison between oral and intravenous administration of bisphosphonates. The researchers suspect that infusion therapy is better tolerated and leads to fewer side effects. The results should help to improve the treatment of osteoporosis in SSc in the long term.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
> 18 years
Confirmed diagnosis of SSc that meets the classification criteria
Indication for osteospecific/biphosphonate therapy
Bone mineral density measurement prior to the start of bisphosphonate therapy
Informed written consent
Exclusion criteria:
Osteospecific therapy prior to study inclusion
Contraindications for therapy with bisphosphonates
Other secondary osteoporosis such as
- Taking glucocorticoids > 5 mg prednisolone equivalent/day
- Diabetes mellitus type I
- Taking growth hormones, estrogens, aromatase inhibitors, other tumor therapy
- Heart failure with a left ventricular ejection fraction < 35%
- Hyperthyroidism (with the exception of hyperthyroidism factitia)
- Chronic renal insufficiency from KDIGO stage G3b (GFR < 45 ml/min/1.73m²)
- Hyperparathyroidism
